content.comment_body: Is it possible and safe to connect 12/24V AC/DC to one relay output and 230V AC to another on a [product_name] base module with 230V supply? The specifications mention 4 relay outputs with a maximum load of 10A.

It is safe as long as the current remains below 10A. As a precaution, it's common practice to use an additional relay to protect the controller outputs from potential damage, especially if something goes wrong with the 230V connection.

To address the question directly: Yes, you can connect 12/24V AC/DC to one relay output and 230V AC to another on a [product_name] base module. The relay terminals are potential-free, meaning they aren't joined internally or to any common potential. The manual's note—'Relay rated voltage 240 VAC/VDC'—refers only to the maximum allowable voltage.

That matches my understanding. I wanted to confirm because in other home automation modules I've used, similar specifications came with warnings against mixing low safety voltages (12V) with higher standard ones (230V) due to the components being close together, which could cause arcing in case of failure. Their certifications require these warnings, so mixing voltages or phases in the same module is not permitted, even though it might work. I wanted to check if [product_name] has a similar safety restriction, or if its construction avoids these issues.

Voltages are not mixed internally. As mentioned, the relay contacts are potential-free, and the insulation distance between terminals is sufficient for 230V. Preventing wiring mistakes that could mix voltages is the responsibility of the installer.
Summing up: it is safe to connect an 8VAC bell to one output and, for example, 230V lights to another output—connections are sufficiently separated both inside and outside the module.
What is your use case with relays in sockets that have a 12VDC coil voltage? Are you switching 230VAC on the contacts, since the coil and contact terminals are located close together?

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion addresses connecting different voltage levels to separate relay outputs on a [product_name] base module. Participants confirm that the relay contacts are potential-free, making it safe to use both low and high voltages on different outputs as long as current ratings and insulation distances are respected. User concerns arise from previous experience with other modules where safety certifications prohibit mixing voltages due to risk of arcing, but it is clarified that [company_name]'s product is designed to ensure sufficient internal separation and documentation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek clear guidance from the manufacturer regarding the safety and compliance of using various voltage levels on different relay outputs within the same [product_name] module, and reassurance that the design prevents electrical hazards experienced with other brands.
